blocks.text: קְרוֹבוֹת לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
uncertainties: This is a running head, not prayer text. The page number 58 is printed on both sides.

blocks.text: ק׳
שְׂרָפִים סוֹבֲבִים יְסַלְסְלוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ:
uncertainties: This page starts in the middle of the piyyut. The earlier lines of this stanza are on s143, which was not assigned to me.
The diacritic dot on שׂ in שְׂרָפִים is small; I read it as a sin dot.
Under the first ב of סוֹבֲבִים I read a hataf-patah, not a sheva. This fits the grammatical convention for two identical consonants in a row, but the mark is faint.
I see no dagesh in the ב of בְקוֹל in any line on this page. The print is too small for me to rule one out entirely.
At the end of each line the sof pasuq is printed as an ornamental colon with a diamond. I transcribed it as ':'.

blocks.text: יְיָ מֶלֶךְ יְיָ מָלָךְ יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד:
uncertainties: לְעֹלָם is spelled defectively, without a vav. The holam dot is faint.
No speaker siglum is printed on any refrain line.

blocks.text: ח׳
עוֹרְכֵי עֹז יַֽעֲנוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מֶלֶךְ:
uncertainties: The holam on עֹז (spelled defectively) is faint.
A short horizontal stroke sits beside the patah under the י of יַֽעֲנוּ. I read it as a meteg. The same stroke appears on יַֽקְדִּישׁוּ, יַֽתְמִידוּ, יַֽתְמִימוּ and יְתַֽנּוּ.

blocks.text: פְּחוּדֵי פְלָאֶיךָ יִפְצְחוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מָלָךְ:
uncertainties: No siglum is printed on this line.
There may be a dagesh in the first פ of פְּחוּדֵי. I can't tell whether the פ of פְלָאֶיךָ also has one.
I read the mark in the final ך of פְלָאֶיךָ as a qamats (pausal form). It could be a sheva.

blocks.text: ק׳
צִבְאוֹת צֹאנֶךָ יְצַלְצְלוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ:
uncertainties: The vowel under the נ of צֹאנֶךָ is clearly a segol (pausal form, not the familiar צֹאנְךָ). I read the mark in the final ך as a qamats, but that is uncertain.

blocks.text: יְיָ מֶלֶךְ יְיָ מָלָךְ יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד:
ח׳
קְהִלּוֹת קֹדֶשׁ יַֽקְדִּישׁוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מֶלֶךְ:
uncertainties: I can't confirm the dagesh in the ל of קְהִלּוֹת or in the ד of יַֽקְדִּישׁוּ.
There is a small mark above יַֽקְדִּישׁוּ near the ד/י. It may be a print artifact.

blocks.text: רִבֲבוֹת רְבָבָה יְרַנֲּנוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מָלָךְ:
uncertainties: No siglum is printed on this line.
I read a hataf-patah under the first ב of רִבֲבוֹת. It could be a sheva.
Under the first נ of יְרַנֲּנוּ the mark could be a hataf-patah or a sheva. I can't confirm the dagesh.

blocks.text: ק׳
שְׁבִיבֵי שַׁלְהֲבוֹת יְשַׁנְּנוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ:
uncertainties: I can't tell whether the vowel under the ה of שַׁלְהֲבוֹת is a hataf-patah, a qamats or a tsere. The familiar spelling is שַׁלְהָבוֹת.
Under the first נ of יְשַׁנְּנוּ I read a sheva, but it could be a hataf-patah. I can't confirm the dagesh.

blocks.text: יְיָ מֶלֶךְ יְיָ מָלָךְ יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד:
ח׳
תּוֹמְכֵי תְהִלּוֹת יַֽתְמִידוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מֶלֶךְ:
uncertainties: I can't confirm the dagesh in the initial ת of תּוֹמְכֵי or in the ל of תְהִלּוֹת.

blocks.text: תּוֹקְפֵי תִפְאַרְתֶּךָ יַֽתְמִימוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ מָלָךְ:
uncertainties: No siglum is printed on this line.
The type is tightly spaced here. The segol under the ת of תִפְאַרְתֶּךָ (pausal form) is clear. The dagesh is uncertain.

blocks.text: קו״ח
uncertainties: This compound siglum is printed directly against the first word. I read it as קו״ח (קהל וחזן, congregation and cantor).

blocks.text: תְּמִימֵי תְעוּדָה יְתַֽנּוּ בְקוֹל. יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ:
uncertainties: For the verb I read יְתַֽנּוּ, with a meteg-like stroke under the ת. The vowels and dagesh are hard to make out; יִתְּנוּ is also possible.
I can't confirm the dagesh in the initial ת of תְּמִימֵי.

blocks.text: יְיָ מֶלֶךְ יְיָ מָלָךְ יְיָ יִמְלֹךְ לְעֹלָם וָעֶד:
uncertainties: This final refrain is printed in a larger type than the earlier refrains.
My assigned scope ends here. The next line, וּבְכֵן דַּיַּן אֱמֶת אַתָּה, and the לאל עורך דין material are excluded.

blocks.text: Morning Prayer for the New Year
uncertainties: This is a running head. The page number 58 is printed on both sides.

blocks.text: The Seraphim around Him glorify aloud: The Lord will reign.
uncertainties: The initial 'T' of 'The' is partly broken or cropped and looks like 'Γhe'. The intended word is 'The'.
This is printed in two columns: the response sits in the right column, level with the second line of the verse.

blocks.text:
The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
Those who classify the law respond aloud: The Lord is King.
Those in dread at Thy wonders utter aloud: The Lord has reigned.
uncertainties: 'won-ders' is hyphenated across the line break in print.

The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,
The Lord will reign for ever and ever.
Holy communities sanctify aloud: The Lord is King.
Myriads of myriads exult aloud: The Lord has reigned.
Those fashioned of flames repeat aloud: The Lord will reign.

The Lord is King, the Lord has reigned,

blocks.text: Those who maintain praises say constantly aloud: The Lord is King.
Those who affirm Thy glory speak sincerely and aloud: The Lord has reigned.
The perfect in testimony relate aloud: The Lord will reign.

notes: I read s144 and s145 in full, plus the enlarged top crops of each. The crops and the full pages show the same lines and I have not duplicated any. Everything in scope on both pages falls inside the crops, so no line was cut.

Page s144 begins in the middle of the piyyut (אדירי איומה). The first line, שְׂרָפִים, closes a triplet whose earlier lines are on s143, which I was not assigned. In the acrostic, the שׂ of שְׂרָפִים stands for the samekh slot. The stanzas that follow carry the letters ע/פ/צ, ק/ר/ש and ת/ת/ת.
Each triplet ends with the responses מֶלֶךְ / מָלָךְ / יִמְלֹךְ in that order, then the full refrain.

Speaker sigla: ח׳ (chazzan) marks the first line of each triplet. ק׳ (congregation) marks the third line. The second line has no siglum. The third line of the final triplet is marked קו״ח (congregation and chazzan). The refrain lines carry no siglum. The English page has no role markings.
The pausal forms פְלָאֶיךָ, צֹאנֶךָ and תִפְאַרְתֶּךָ, and the hataf-patah under the first of two identical consonants (סוֹבֲבִים, רִבֲבוֹת), are left as printed and not normalized.
There are no Rashi rubrics, citations or conditional alternatives in this section. Every Hebrew line has its English counterpart, and no English is missing.
I found no definite source typos, so I am proposing no corrections. The marks I could not resolve are listed in each block's uncertainties.
